yerba-mate.name: Yerba mate
yerba-mate.summary: A holly species native to South America whose leaves are steeped to make the drink mate, first cultivated by the indigenous Guaraní before European colonization and later spread widely after Jesuits saw its commercial potential.

misiones-province.name: Misiones Province
misiones-province.summary: A province in northeastern Argentina that was an early center of Jesuit missionary activity beginning in the early 17th century.

corrientes-province.name: Corrientes Province
corrientes-province.summary: A province in northeast Argentina's Mesopotamia region, one of the country's oldest and one of the fourteen founding provinces of the Argentine Confederation.

francisco-de-orellana.name: Francisco de Orellana
francisco-de-orellana.summary: Spanish explorer and conquistador (1511–1546) who became the first known person to sail the length of the Amazon River, in 1542, and founded the city of Guayaquil.

maraj.name: Marajó
maraj.summary: A large island in Pará, Brazil, at the mouth of the Amazon, site from roughly 400 BCE to 1600 CE of the advanced pre-Cabraline Marajoara society.

feijoada.name: Feijoada
feijoada.summary: A bean stew with beef or pork found across the Portuguese-speaking world, made with white, black or red beans and usually served with rice.

casabe.name: Casabe
casabe.summary: A flatbread made from cassava, eaten across the Caribbean and Amazon since before European contact and recognized as UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2024.

minas-gerais.name: Minas Gerais
minas-gerais.summary: A landlocked Brazilian state in the Southeast Region, the fourth largest by area and second most populous, whose capital is Belo Horizonte.

manoel-da-costa-ata-de.name: Manoel da Costa Ataíde
manoel-da-costa-ata-de.summary: A Brazilian painter, sculptor, gilder and teacher (1762-1830), a major figure of the baroque-rococo school in Minas Gerais known for bright colors, especially blue.

aleijadinho.name: Aleijadinho
aleijadinho.summary: Sculptor, carver and architect of Colonial Brazil (c. 1730/1738–1814), regarded as the greatest exponent of Brazilian Baroque colonial art.

reductions.name: Reductions
reductions.summary: Settlements in which Spanish colonial rulers and Catholic missionaries forcibly relocated Indigenous peoples of the Americas and the Philippines to control and evangelize them, most successfully by Jesuits in Paraguay.

joseph-of-anchieta.name: José de Anchieta
joseph-of-anchieta.summary: Spanish Jesuit missionary to colonial Brazil (1534–1597) who helped found São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro and is considered the father of Brazilian literature; later canonized a saint.

ouro-preto.name: Ouro Preto
ouro-preto.summary: A former colonial gold-mining town in Brazil's Minas Gerais, once called Vila Rica, that served as the state's capital from 1720 to 1897 and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its Baroque architecture.

emerico-lobo-de-mesquita.name: Lobo de Mesquita
emerico-lobo-de-mesquita.summary: A Brazilian composer and organist active in colonial Minas Gerais in the late 1700s, known for sacred choral music written for churches and religious brotherhoods.

francisco-gomes-da-rocha.name: Francisco Gomes da Rocha
francisco-gomes-da-rocha.summary: Brazilian composer, singer and bassoonist (1745–1808), a leading musician of Vila Rica (now Ouro Preto) and successor to Lobo de Mesquita; only 5 of his roughly 200 works survive.

tom-s-ant-nio-gonzaga.name: Tomás António Gonzaga
tom-s-ant-nio-gonzaga.summary: Portuguese Neoclassic poet (1744–c.1810) who worked as a colonial official in Brazil and wrote love poetry under the pen name Dirceu.

cl-udio-manuel-da-costa.name: Cláudio Manuel da Costa
cl-udio-manuel-da-costa.summary: Brazilian poet and musician (1729-1789) credited with introducing Neoclassicism to Brazil, best known for the epic poem Vila Rica.

ricardo-do-pilar.name: Ricardo do Pilar
ricardo-do-pilar.summary: German-born Brazilian monk and painter (1635–1700) who worked for the Monastery of St. Benedict in Rio de Janeiro, mainly painting portraits of saints and monks.

dutch-brazil.name: Dutch Brazil
dutch-brazil.summary: Dutch colony in northeastern Brazil, also called New Holland, controlled from 1630 to 1654 with its capital at Recife before being ceded back to Portugal in 1661.

francesco-borromini.name: Francesco Borromini
francesco-borromini.summary: Italian architect (1599-1667), a leading figure alongside Bernini and Cortona in the emergence of Roman Baroque architecture, known for inventive, idiosyncratic designs.

john-maurice-prince-of-nassau-siegen.name: John Maurice of Nassau
john-maurice-prince-of-nassau-siegen.summary: Count, later Prince, of Nassau-Siegen, nicknamed 'the Brazilian' for his period as governor of Dutch Brazil; his former Hague residence is now the Mauritshuis museum.

olinda.name: Olinda
olinda.summary: Historic Brazilian city near Recife, former capital of colonial Pernambuco, known for its well-preserved architecture (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) and street Carnaval.

giuseppe-antonio-landi.name: Antônio José Landi
giuseppe-antonio-landi.summary: An 18th-century Italian neoclassical architect and painter (1713–1791) whose works included churches and palaces built during his time in colonial Brazil.

bel-m.name: Belém
bel-m.summary: The capital of Pará state in northern Brazil and gateway to the Amazon River, founded in 1616 as the first European colony on the Amazon.

dutch-west-india-company.name: Dutch West India Company
dutch-west-india-company.summary: Dutch chartered company founded in 1621, given a monopoly on trade and colonisation across West Africa and the Americas, including a role in the Atlantic slave trade.

dutch-portuguese-war.name: Dutch–Portuguese War
dutch-portuguese-war.summary: Global conflict beginning in 1598 in which Dutch trading companies fought Portugal and the Iberian Union for colonies in the Americas, Africa and Asia, nicknamed the Spice War.

s-o-lu-s-maranh-o.name: São Luís
s-o-lu-s-maranh-o.summary: Capital of the Brazilian state of Maranhão, founded by France as Saint-Louis-de-Maragnan and the only Brazilian state capital founded by that country; its 17th-century historic center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

philip-ii-of-spain.name: Philip II of Spain
philip-ii-of-spain.summary: King of Spain from 1556 and Portugal from 1580, under whom Spain reached its height of power, including the conquest of the Philippines, named in his honor.

colonia-del-sacramento.name: Colonia del Sacramento
colonia-del-sacramento.summary: A city in southwestern Uruguay founded by the Portuguese in 1680, long disputed between Portugal and Spain, whose historic quarter is now a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

banda-oriental.name: Banda Oriental
banda-oriental.summary: The historical name for territories east of the Uruguay River and north of the Río de la Plata, now Uruguay and parts of Brazil, disputed between the Spanish and Portuguese empires.

aqualtune.name: Aqualtune
aqualtune.summary: Kongo princess (fl. 1665-75) who led ten thousand fighters at the Battle of Mbwila, was later enslaved in Brazil, escaped, and led a settlement within the Palmares quilombo; grandmother of Zumbi.

ganga-zumba.name: Ganga Zumba
ganga-zumba.summary: First leader (c. 1630-1678) of Quilombo dos Palmares, a settlement of escaped enslaved people in Brazil, having himself escaped a sugar plantation to rise to its highest authority.

palmares-quilombo.name: Quilombo dos Palmares
palmares-quilombo.summary: A community of escaped slaves in colonial Brazil, located in what is now Alagoas, that existed from 1605 until it was suppressed in 1694.

treaty-of-tordesillas.name: Treaty of Tordesillas
treaty-of-tordesillas.summary: 1494 treaty dividing newly discovered lands outside Europe between Portugal and Castile along a meridian west of Cape Verde.

pope-alexander-vi.name: Pope Alexander VI
pope-alexander-vi.summary: Born Rodrigo Borgia, head of the Catholic Church from 1492 to 1503; his 1493 bulls confirmed Spanish rights in the New World after Columbus's 1492 voyage.

pero-vaz-de-caminha.name: Pero Vaz de Caminha
pero-vaz-de-caminha.summary: A Portuguese knight who accompanied Pedro Álvares Cabral to India in 1500 and wrote the official report describing the discovery of Brazil.

manuel-i-of-portugal.name: Manuel I of Portugal
manuel-i-of-portugal.summary: King of Portugal from 1495 to 1521, known as the Fortunate, whose reign saw major overseas expansion including Vasco da Gama's sea route to India and Cabral's discovery of Brazil.

greg-rio-de-matos.name: Gregório de Matos
greg-rio-de-matos.summary: A Portuguese Baroque poet from colonial Brazil (1636 to 1696), called the founder of Brazilian literature, known for satirical poems against the Catholic Church that earned him the nickname 'Boca do Inferno' (Hell's Mouth).

luis-de-g-ngora.name: Luis de Góngora
luis-de-g-ngora.summary: A Spanish Baroque poet and Catholic priest (1561-1627), considered alongside his rival Francisco de Quevedo among the greatest Spanish poets; his ornate style became known as Gongorismo.

francisco-de-quevedo.name: Francisco de Quevedo
francisco-de-quevedo.summary: Spanish nobleman, politician and Baroque-era writer (1580–1645), one of the most prominent Spanish poets of his age, known for his rivalry with Luis de Góngora.

jean-de-l-ry.name: Jean de Léry
jean-de-l-ry.summary: A French explorer, writer and Reformed pastor (1534/36–1613) who joined a Protestant colony in Brazil in 1557–58 and wrote an account of the voyage, including early transcriptions of Tupinambá music.

hans-staden.name: Hans Staden
hans-staden.summary: German soldier and explorer (c. 1525–1576) captured by the Tupinambá in Brazil, whose widely read account of his captivity claimed the people who held him practiced cannibalism.

tupi-people.name: Tupi people
tupi-people.summary: One of the largest Indigenous groups in Brazil before European colonization, who migrated from the Amazon and settled along the Atlantic coast beginning around 1,000 years ago.

ant-nio-vieira.name: António Vieira
ant-nio-vieira.summary: Portuguese Jesuit priest, diplomat, orator and philosopher (1608–1697) who served on the Royal Council to the King of Portugal.

bas-lio-da-gama.name: Basílio da Gama
bas-lio-da-gama.summary: A colonial Brazilian Jesuit poet (1740–1795), famous for the epic poem O Uraguai, written under the pen name Termindo Sipílio.

jesuit-missions-among-the-guaran.name: Guarany Missions
jesuit-missions-among-the-guaran.summary: Settlements set up by the Jesuit order for the Guaraní people across what are now Argentina, Brazil and Paraguay, running from the early 1600s until the Jesuits' expulsion from the Americas in the late 1700s.

alexandre-rodrigues-ferreira.name: Alexandre Rodrigues Ferreira
alexandre-rodrigues-ferreira.summary: A Portuguese naturalist born in Brazil (1756–1815) who journeyed across the Amazon Basin to Mato Grosso between 1783 and 1792, documenting its flora, fauna and peoples.

marquis-of-pombal-title.name: Marquis of Pombal
marquis-of-pombal-title.summary: Title held by Sebastião José de Carvalho e Melo, Portugal's chief minister under King Joseph I, created in 1769 after he had already been made Count of Oeiras in 1759.

lisbon-academy-of-sciences.name: Lisbon Academy of Sciences
lisbon-academy-of-sciences.summary: Portugal's national academy for advancing sciences and learning, and the country's official regulator of the Portuguese language.

federal-university-of-rio-de-janeiro.name: Federal University of Rio de Janeiro
federal-university-of-rio-de-janeiro.summary: Brazil's largest federal university and first official higher education institution, operating continuously since 1792, when its engineering-school precursor was founded in Rio de Janeiro.
federal-university-of-rio-de-janeiro.source_title: Federal University of Rio de Janeiro

instituto-militar-de-engenharia.name: Military Institute of Engineering
instituto-militar-de-engenharia.summary: Engineering institute maintained by the Brazilian Army in Rio de Janeiro, ranked as the oldest and one of the best engineering schools in Brazil.

tienne-geoffroy-saint-hilaire.name: Étienne Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire
tienne-geoffroy-saint-hilaire.summary: French naturalist (1772–1844) who developed theories of the unity of animal design and defended Lamarck's evolutionary ideas, now seen as a forerunner of evo-devo.

inconfid-ncia-mineira.name: Inconfidência Mineira
inconfid-ncia-mineira.summary: An unsuccessful 1789 separatist plot in colonial Brazil, driven by declining gold mining and new taxes and partly inspired by American independence.

pedro-lvares-cabral.name: Pedro Álvares Cabral
pedro-lvares-cabral.summary: Portuguese nobleman and navigator (c. 1467–c. 1520) regarded as the European discoverer of Brazil, leading a 1500 expedition that touched four continents.

john-iv-of-portugal.name: John IV of Portugal
john-iv-of-portugal.summary: King of Portugal from 1640 to 1656, proclaimed king as the Portuguese Restoration War began, ending 60 years of union with Spain; the empire reached its greatest extent under him.

portuguese-restoration-war.name: Portuguese Restoration War
portuguese-restoration-war.summary: The 1641–1668 conflict between Portugal and Spain that ended the Iberian Union and established the House of Braganza as Portugal's ruling dynasty.

iberian-union.name: Iberian Union
iberian-union.summary: The 1580–1640 personal union under Spain's Habsburg kings joining the crowns of Portugal, Castile and Aragon, ended when Portugal's Braganza dynasty broke away.

tamoio-people.name: Tamoio
tamoio-people.summary: Tupi-speaking indigenous group of Brazil's coast around Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo, numbering roughly 70,000 at the time of European contact.

mem-de-s.name: Mem de Sá
mem-de-s.summary: Governor-General of Portuguese Brazil from 1557 to 1572, who backed Jesuit missionaries and opposed plantation owners' enslavement of indigenous people.

france-antarctique.name: France Antarctique
france-antarctique.summary: A French colony at what is now Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, existing from 1555 to 1567, that became a Huguenot haven before being destroyed by the Portuguese.

guanabara-bay.name: Guanabara Bay
guanabara-bay.summary: A large bay in Rio de Janeiro state, Brazil, bordered by the cities of Rio de Janeiro and Niterói.

est-cio-de-s.name: Estácio de Sá
est-cio-de-s.summary: Portuguese soldier (1520–1567) sent to fight French colonists in Brazil, who founded the city of Rio de Janeiro in 1567.

governorate-general-of-brazil.name: Governorate General of Brazil
governorate-general-of-brazil.summary: A Portuguese colonial administration over Brazil equivalent to a viceroyalty, whose governors general reported directly to the crown and oversaw the colony's royal captaincies.

state-of-gr-o-par-and-maranh-o.name: Grão-Pará and Maranhão
state-of-gr-o-par-and-maranh-o.summary: A state of the Portuguese Empire, formed in colonial Brazil.

mauritsstad.name: Mauritsstad
mauritsstad.summary: Capital of Dutch Brazil, today part of the Brazilian city of Recife.

eighty-years-war.name: Eighty Years' War
eighty-years-war.summary: Also called the Dutch Revolt, an armed conflict from around 1566 to 1648 between Dutch rebels and the Spanish government, ending in recognition of the Dutch Republic.

twelve-years-truce.name: Twelve Years' Truce
twelve-years-truce.summary: A 1609–1621 ceasefire in the Eighty Years' War between Spain and the Dutch Republic, letting Spain focus resources elsewhere without yet formally recognizing Dutch independence.

tiradentes.name: Tiradentes
tiradentes.summary: Leading figure in the Inconfidência Mineira, a movement to make colonial Brazil an independent republic; arrested, tried and publicly hanged in 1792, he later became a national hero of Brazil.

guaran-people.name: Guaraní people
guaran-people.summary: An indigenous South American people, numbering around 280,000, living mainly in Paraguay, Argentina, Brazil and Bolivia, whose language remains an official language of Paraguay.

philip-iii-of-spain.name: Philip III of Spain
philip-iii-of-spain.summary: King of Spain and Portugal from 1598 to 1621, whose reign brought relative peace to Western Europe though power was mostly delegated to his chief minister, the Duke of Lerma.

asunci-n.name: Asunción
asunci-n.summary: Capital and largest city of Paraguay, one of the oldest cities in South America, from which Spanish expeditions departed to found many other cities including Buenos Aires.

pope-innocent-xi.name: Pope Innocent XI
pope-innocent-xi.summary: Head of the Catholic Church and Papal States from 1676 to 1689, known for frugal, reforming governance and financial support for freeing Hungary from Ottoman rule.

treaty-of-the-mapu.name: Treaty of the Mapuá
treaty-of-the-mapu.summary: Peace treaty sworn in August 1659 between Portuguese Jesuits and indigenous peoples of the Marajó Archipelago, ending Dutch ambitions there but collapsing within two years after a colonist revolt over slave labor.

nhamund-river.name: Nhamundá River
nhamund-river.summary: A roughly 300 km river in northern Brazil, marking part of the border between Amazonas and Pará states, that joins the Trombetas River shortly before it meets the Amazon.

cosmas-and-damian.name: Cosmas and Damian
cosmas-and-damian.summary: Twin Arab physicians and early Christian martyrs (3rd century-c. 287/303 AD) who treated patients without charging fees and were executed during the Diocletian persecution.

saint-george.name: Saint George
saint-george.summary: Early Christian martyr who died in 303, said to have been a soldier in the Roman army executed for refusing to renounce his faith; widely venerated and claimed as patron saint by many countries and cities.

ogun.name: Ogun
ogun.summary: A major deity in Yoruba religion associated with war, iron and metalworking, also venerated in African diaspora religions such as Santería and Candomblé.

saint-barbara.name: Saint Barbara
saint-barbara.summary: An early Christian martyr from Heliopolis (modern Baalbek, Lebanon), venerated especially in the East since the 9th century as patron saint of armourers, miners and mathematicians.

benedict-the-moor.name: Benedict the Moor
benedict-the-moor.summary: Afro-Sicilian Franciscan friar (1526–1589), born to enslaved parents and freed at birth, known for his charity; canonized in 1807.

kaleb-of-axum.name: Kaleb of Axum
kaleb-of-axum.summary: A king of Aksum, a kingdom in what is now Ethiopia and Eritrea, also known and venerated under other names including Saint Elesbaan and Ella Asbeha.

ephigenia-of-ethiopia.name: Saint Ephigenia
ephigenia-of-ethiopia.summary: A Western folk saint described in the Golden Legend as a virgin from Ethiopia, converted to Christianity and consecrated to God by Matthew the Apostle.

escrava-anastacia.name: Escrava Anastácia
escrava-anastacia.summary: An enslaved woman of African descent venerated as a Brazilian folk saint, depicted with piercing blue eyes and an iron facemask, though not officially recognized by the Catholic Church.

maranh-o.name: Maranhão
maranh-o.summary: A state in northeastern Brazil with about 7 million people, bordering the Atlantic Ocean, home to the dunes of Lençóis and the UNESCO World Heritage city of São Luís.
